text: The Fed just hiked rates to 4.00–4.25% with another possible hike in December, while CPI is stuck at 3.4% and payrolls came in red-hot at 162,000 — this means borrowing costs are rising again, which is especially painful for unprofitable growth stocks in your portfolio.
IONQ is down 10.6%, unprofitable, 46% off its high with 10% short interest — trim your position to reduce exposure to another speculative, cash-burning quantum name while rates are heading higher.
MSTR is 55% off its high with deeply negative cash flow and is essentially a leveraged Bitcoin bet — trim to a size you'd be comfortable losing entirely, because this is speculation, not investing.

Google trades at a reasonable PE of 22 with 15% revenue growth and strong free cash flow — it's the kind of profitable, cash-rich company that holds up well when rates rise, so adding here makes sense.
UnitedHealth is down 12.3% but its MACD is turning bullish and the fundamentals remain strong — this pullback in a defensive healthcare giant is a reasonable spot to add shares.
